@ryangamerdev Thanks for the quick follow-up — switching the PR to `Related: #41358` instead of `Closes` is exactly the right call. That keeps the summary/goal-preservation half tracked by the PR and leaves the session-loop concurrency/confirmation-barrier half open here, so neither gap becomes orphaned.

The three points your PR adds are genuinely important for our setup:
- **Ratios overriding hard tokens when set** — we hit the "small session gets fully summarized, nothing kept verbatim" case (a session smaller than `preserve_recent_tokens` ends up `keep.start === 0`), so an `extract_ratio`/`recent_ratio` that scales with the conversation directly fixes that.
- **Trigger relative to the context window** — our runs mix small- and large-context models with one config, so a fixed `reserved` headroom triggering very differently per model is a real pain; `trigger_ratio` fixes the scaling.
- **"Recent" session context in the summary** — this is the part we believe keeps the task goal/direction across the boundary.

We'll test on Windows Desktop against both local sidecar and remote models once a build is available, and report measured before/after drift behavior back to this PR. Thanks for the structured compaction v2 critique too — the head|tail analysis matches what we observed.

Same thing bricked several of my sessions (Kimi K3 behind a litellm gateway). Until the core fix in #45839 lands, you can work around it with a small plugin that hooks `experimental.chat.messages.transform` and sanitizes replayed history before conversion — it drops empty `text` parts and step segments that contain only reasoning (which OpenAI-compatible providers drop, producing the empty assistant message): https://github.com/impptg/opencode-fix-empty-assistant-messages

For an already-bricked session: the stored history in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` needs a cleanup (delete empty text parts / reasoning-only step segments of the offending assistant messages), then restart the client. Once #45839 is merged the plugin can be removed — conversion-time filtering also heals bricked sessions automatically.

Hit the same failure family (Kimi K3 via an OpenAI-compatible gateway). While waiting for the core fix (#45839), this plugin works around it at send time — it hooks `experimental.chat.messages.transform` and drops empty `text` parts plus reasoning-only step segments from replayed history so no empty assistant message reaches the wire: https://github.com/impptg/opencode-fix-empty-assistant-messages

Note it only prevents *new* requests from failing; a session whose stored history is already poisoned needs a one-time DB cleanup (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) or the upstream fix, which heals old sessions at conversion time. Plugin is removable once #45839 ships.

For anyone landing here from search: this error means the replayed history contains an assistant message that serializes with empty content (typically from a mid-turn abort or empty streamed text parts with reasoning models like Kimi K3), and strict providers reject the whole request — bricking the session.

Two fixes:
- Temporary workaround: https://github.com/impptg/opencode-fix-empty-assistant-messages — an opencode plugin that sanitizes history via the `experimental.chat.messages.transform` hook before each request (drops empty text parts and reasoning-only step segments).
- Permanent fix: #45839 (pending review) filters these at conversion time in core, which also heals already-bricked sessions. Once it's released, remove the plugin.

If your session is already bricked and you can't wait: clean the offending assistant rows in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (empty text parts / reasoning-only steps), then restart the client.

Related failure family (I hit it with Kimi K3 behind a litellm gateway): assistant turns that replay with empty content get rejected by strict providers and brick the session.

A send-time workaround that may help depending on your exact shape: https://github.com/impptg/opencode-fix-empty-assistant-messages — a plugin hooking `experimental.chat.messages.transform` that drops empty `text` parts and reasoning-only step segments from replayed history (the two shapes I confirmed producing `content: ""` on the wire). Tool-call-only turns are kept intact, so if your empty-content turn truly carries `tool_calls`, this plugin alone won't change that frame.

The general fix is pending upstream in #45839 (filters assistant turns with no model-visible content at conversion time, which also heals already-bricked sessions).

Additional detail that narrows the reproduction: **closing the project in Desktop and re-opening the directory at its new path does not recover either.**

As far as I can tell this is because `Project.fromDirectory` resolves the project via the stable id cached in `.git/opencode`. Opening the *new* path hits that cache, resolves to the *existing* `project` row, and returns it with its stale `worktree` (old path) — so the freshly re-added project maps straight back to the broken row and keeps failing with the same ENOENT. There is no UI-only path to recovery; the stale `worktree` column has to be corrected (or the row removed) in the DB.

So the move-migration gap is: id resolution and `project_directory`/sessions get updated/reused on a move, but `project.worktree` never does, and it's the column the Desktop uses to open the repo.

Pre-merge performance and memory review: no blocker found in the measured workloads.

- A live-clock probe observed at most one active timer child per text fragment and zero after flushing. Installed Effect 4.0.0-rc.112 removes completed children immediately and cancels native timeouts on interruption.

- Before/after microbenchmarks (Bun 1.4.0, Windows, cheap non-retaining publish sink): 100,000 chunk appends took 151.24 ms before versus 99.86 ms after. 5,000 one-chunk fragments took 82.34 ms before versus 106.33 ms after, an added 4.8 microseconds per short fragment from timer creation/cancellation.
- A separate 80,000-fragment memory probe showed nearly identical post-GC heap growth: 149.6 KiB before versus 151.9 KiB after. Transient heap use increased, as expected from timer/fiber allocations.
- All 204 focused Core tests passed again.

Hey! Your PR title `feat(desktop,session-ui): collapsible reasoning cards` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

Where `scope` is the package name (e.g., `app`, `desktop`, `opencode`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.

### Real-world case

We observed this behavior on OpenCode `1.18.25` with an OpenAI-compatible local provider:

| Event | Result |
|---|---|
| Completed agent steps | 17 normal tool-driven steps |
| Final response duration | Approximately 13 minutes |
| Configured output limit | `16,384` tokens |
| Actual output | Exactly `16,384` tokens |
| Provider finish reason | `length` |
| OpenCode behavior | Logged `exiting loop` and left the unfinished task idle |

The model server stayed healthy, and the same session remained resumable through a manual **Continue** message. The interruption was specifically caused by OpenCode treating `length` as a terminal success instead of a truncation signal.

### Why raising the limit is not enough

Increasing `maxOutputTokens` only postpones the same failure. It can also waste substantially more generation time before OpenCode silently stops.

### Suggested behavior

When a response ends with `finish_reason: "length"`, OpenCode should:

1. Show a visible notice that the response reached its output limit.
2. Add a concise synthetic continuation instruction.
3. Continue within the **same session**, preserving conversation state and provider-side prompt-cache reuse.
4. Limit consecutive automatic continuations to prevent runaway reasoning or repetition.
5. If that safety limit is reached, stop with an explicit, actionable error instead of recording a normal completion.

A bounded automatic continuation would preserve autonomous task execution without creating an uncontrolled loop.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| OpenCode | `1.18.25` |
| Provider | OpenAI-compatible local endpoint backed by `mlx_lm.server` |
| Model | Qwen3.8 27B |
| Configured output limit | `16,384` tokens |
| Cached input on the affected request | Approximately `117,666` tokens |

### What happened

1. The agent completed **17 normal steps**, including successful tool calls.
2. Step 18 ran for approximately **13 minutes**.
3. That response produced exactly **16,384 output tokens**, matching the configured ceiling.
4. OpenCode stored the assistant message as `finish: "length"`.
5. The next log entry was `exiting loop`.
6. The task was still unfinished, but the session became idle without an error or continuation prompt.

### What the evidence rules out

The model server remained healthy throughout the event:

- No provider crash
- No process restart
- No out-of-memory event
- No context-window overflow

The same session accepted a later manual continuation, confirming that it remained valid and resumable.

### Why long-running tasks may appear unaffected

Other tasks have run for hours because they used many separate tool-call rounds. Each response stayed below the per-response output ceiling, so OpenCode kept looping.

In this case, a single reasoning/generation turn exhausted the full output allowance. OpenCode then treated `length` as successful completion, even though it indicates truncation.

### User-visible result

**Expected:** OpenCode should report truncation and continue, or explicitly ask for intervention.

**Actual:** OpenCode silently stopped an unfinished task after spending approximately 13 minutes on the truncated response.

Confirmed on Windows with opencode desktop 1.18.25. I observed the inline per-turn Changed files card leak into a session that only produced a conversational response while another session edited a file in the same directory.

The backend logs make the ordering clear: session B captures its initial snapshot, session A edits the file while B is still streaming, then B completes and its whole-worktree end snapshot includes the edit from A. This is not only the app git review cache/file-watcher path described above. The per-turn summary itself is vulnerable:

- packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts: SessionProcessor.create calls snapshot.track() before streaming and again on step-finish.
- packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts: computeDiff calls snapshot.diffFull(from, to) for those whole-worktree hashes.
- packages/opencode/src/snapshot/index.ts: snapshots share a gitdir keyed by project/worktree and stage all changed/untracked files in the directory.

Therefore any external or concurrent-session edit between the two snapshots is attributed to that turn and persisted in target.info.summary.diffs. Adding sessionID only to the frontend VCS cache key will not fix this inline card. Filtering by turnDiffs is also insufficient because turnDiffs already contains the leaked file.

A safe local mitigation is snapshot: false, which removes misleading cards but also disables snapshot-based summaries/revert. A complete fix needs session-owned mutation attribution, such as files recorded by mutating tool calls, or isolated per-session worktrees. The implementation also needs defined behavior for shell commands and external processes that modify files.
